How the Digital Library Works

Adding a book

Only a title is required. The "link" field is optional — fill it in only if the book is already hosted somewhere online (Google Drive, Dropbox, etc.). If it's just a file on your own computer, leave it blank; the book still works fine without one.

Adding the file

Pick the PDF file when adding or editing a book, and the browser reads its text right there and indexes it for search. The file itself then uploads to your own account's private cloud storage (files up to 50 MB — a Supabase Free plan limit, not one this app chose) — nobody else can reach it — which is what lets the book open from any device you're logged into, not just the one you added it on. It also remembers a copy right in this browser on this device, so opening it here never needs a network round-trip. A book with a bigger file still saves fine, just without that cloud/cross-device copy — an external link works regardless of size.

The badges on each book tell you where it stands: Searchable means its text has been indexed, Not indexed means it hasn't yet, and ☁️ Cloud means the actual file uploaded successfully and will open on any device. A book with none of these still works fine — those badges are about search and cross-device opening, not whether the book itself is useful.

Searching

Type in the search box to search the actual text of every indexed book, not just titles. Each matching book shows one or more highlighted excerpts of the surrounding text so you can see the match in context — scroll inside a book's card if it has more than a few.

Opening a book

Click a book's title, or a highlighted search excerpt, and it tries these in order, doing whichever one actually applies:

  • Opens right inside the app, jumped to the right page, from this device's own remembered copy if it has one — instant, and works offline.
  • Opens right inside the app from your account's cloud copy otherwise, if the file was uploaded from any device.
  • Opens your online link at that page in a new tab (search results only — a title click never falls back to this) if there's no local or cloud copy but the book has a link.
  • Explains there's nothing to open yet if none of the above apply.

Inside the viewer

Prev / Next flip pages; the − / + buttons zoom in and out.

📂 Save Local Copy

Optional, and no longer required for a book to follow you across devices — the cloud copy handles that. This just caches the file's own bytes right in THIS browser, on THIS device, so it opens instantly (and works offline) without fetching the cloud copy every time. Find it inside Edit for a book that's already saved. Clicking it again later just refreshes this device's cached copy.
